snippet.title: Why was this kung fu masterpiece banned? - Gladys Mac
snippet.description:
Get to know Jin Yong’s “Legend of the Condor Heroes,” an epic tale of adventure and war, romance, brotherhood and betrayal.

--

In the 1950s, citizens flocked to newsstands to pick up the latest edition of a story set hundreds of years in the past — a multigenerational tale of adventure and war, romance and intrigue, brotherhood and betrayal. Jin Yong’s epic "Legend of the Condor Heroes" is considered one of Hong Kong’s most important works of fiction. Gladys Mac digs into this beloved sweeping saga of the steppes.

Why did Kronos eat his children? Was he a paranoid monster like in God of War, or was there a deeper reason in Greek mythology?

In this video from Yours Mythically, we break down the shocking difference between Kronos in God of War and the real Kronos from Greek mythology.

In God of War, Kronos is shown as a cruel, broken Titan who devours his children out of fear and is later punished by Zeus to carry Pandora’s Temple. He is ultimately killed by Kratos in a brutal confrontation.

But in Greek mythology, Kronos ruled during the Golden Age, a time of peace and abundance. His decision to swallow his children was driven by prophecy and the fear of being overthrown, not mindless rage. Some versions of the myth even say he was later freed and allowed to rule Elysium.

Discover the real reason Kronos ate his children and how God of War reimagined one of the most powerful Titans in mythology.

snippet.title: Japanese Response to The Potsdam Declaration #ww2
snippet.description:
The declaration would be issued on July 26th 1945, however after the first day, there was still no response. Even after the second day and then a third, there was still no response, the Allies would hear nothing.

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Suzuki, the Japanese, considering the terms of the Potsdam Declaration unacceptable and still unwilling to surrender, had chosen to enact a policy of mokusatsu (黙殺), or “killing with silence”, deciding to ignore the ultimatum altogether. 

To the Japanese, giving no response at all, was in fact a response, it was a complete dismissal of the terms. This would leave Truman with very few options. He would now have to consider using the Atomic Bomb, with many factors weighing on his mind.

snippet.title: Just how ancient is sumo? - Lee Thompson
snippet.description:
Trace the history of sumo, and explore how the sport was designed and modified to reflect ancient Japan’s culture and traditions.

--

Sumo wrestling is known across the world as a beloved form of entertainment, a grand display of strength, and an ode to Japan's ancient past and traditions. But surprisingly, many of these so-called "ancient" traditions were actually recent inventions. So, what were these fabricated practices, and how do they relate to sumo’s true history? Lee Thompson traces the evolution of the sport.

Dig into the vast and wild world of fungi, and explore how these organisms evolved to play a range of essential ecological roles.

The diverse fungal kingdom, which includes everything from baker’s yeast to edible mushrooms to foot infections, has long defied assumptions. Scientists estimate that somewhere between 2 and 12 million species of fungi remain undiscovered— either because they’re microscopic, live hidden within other species, or for other unknown reasons. Max G. Levy digs into the vast and wild world of fungi.

snippet.title: GREEK MYTHOLOGY - The Entire Story
snippet.description:
For three thousand years, Greek Mythology and the myths of ancient Greece have shaped the world we live in, serving as the inspiration behind countless works of art, literature, film, and music, as well as being one of the very foundations of Western culture.

In this video, we (Deep Dive History) present to you the most comprehensive Greek Mythology documentary ever made: The Entire Story of Greek Mythology, from the very beginning of creation to the Age of Iron, the end of the Mythological story. Not only is the video narrated by the world-class, award-winning voice of British actor David Rintoul, we take you along this grand adventure, with classical paintings, animated maps, 3D rendered models, 4k animated family trees, custom artwork and a musical score to help you get lost in the story. 

Every Greek myth is covered, from the birth of the universe out of Chaos, to the rise of the Olympian Gods such as Zeus and Poseidon, to legendary heroes like Heracles and Perseus who defined their age. No myth is left untold. No story is left behind. So sit back, relax, and enjoy the greatest Greek Mythology Documentary ever made.

snippet.title: Truman warns Japan more Atomic Bombs are to come #ww2
snippet.description:
In just a couple of seconds, more than half of Hiroshima had been eviscerated and some 80,000 civilians had perished. Many more would die in the following days, weeks, and years, as severe burns and the harmful effects of radiation began to take its toll. 

Following the bombing, Truman would release a message, broadcasting a warning to Japan live for the world to hear:

*"If they do not now accept our terms, they may expect a rain of ruin from the air, the like of which has never been seen on this earth. Behind this air attack will follow sea and land forces in such numbers and power as they have not yet seen and with the fighting skill of which they are already well aware."*

Radio messages were also broadcast to Japan every 15 minutes, warning that more cities would be targeted unless an immediate surrender was received, and urging Japanese civilians to evacuate all major cities before they fell to the same fate as Hiroshima. 3 days would pass, and yet, with all this destruction, with all this loss of life, there were still no 
signs of Japanese willingness to surrender.

snippet.title: 2. THE TROJAN WAR - The Entire Story
snippet.description:
The Trojan War, immortalised in Homer's Iliad, is one of the greatest and most influential tales of Greek mythology and Western literature, with its story having been told on nearly every corner of the globe. For ten years, the mightiest warriors of Greece laid siege to Troy, the richest city in Asia, fighting for honour, glory, and Helen, a stolen queen. It was a war sparked by love and pride, where gods descended from Olympus to fight alongside mortals and heroes earned immortality through their deeds on the battlefield. At its centre stood Achilles, the greatest warrior who ever lived, a man whose rage nearly destroyed his own allies, and Hector, prince of Troy, whose courage and skill could not save his people from their fate. When the city finally fell to a giant wooden horse through Greek cunning and deception, the age of heroes came to its end in blood, fire, and ash.
